Updates `lint-staged` from 17.5.1 to 17.6.0
Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.6.0

Minor Changes

  • #1850 938d3f4 - Task functions like { title, task } can now use a logger function log() to emit output while the task runs. By default, the output will only be visible if the task fails, unless the --verbose option was used. Additionally, when the task rejects, the error will be shown in the output.

    import { defineConfig } from 'lint-staged/config'

    export default defineConfig({
'*': {
title: 'Fail if PDF files are committed',
task: async (filepaths, { log }) => {
const pdfFiles = filepaths.filter((f) => f.toLowerCase().endsWith('.pdf'))
if (pdfFiles.length > 0) {
log('PDF files should not be committed: %s', pdfFiles)
throw new Error('Failed')
}
},
},
})

  • #1854 30562bc - lint-staged now stages changes to all tracked files modified by tasks, including files that weren’t originally staged or didn’t match the configured globs. This can happen when your task has side-effects, or it's a function that ignores the staged files like () => "prettier --write .".

    If you have unstaged changes in a file and the task also edits that file, your unstaged changes will be staged too. Use --hide-unstaged to hide your changes while tasks run.

Patch Changes

  • #1860 4296532 - The assignment of staged files to lint-staged configuration files (when using multiple, for example in a monorepo) has been rewritten to be more efficient. As a reminder, each staged file is assigned to exactly one configuration (the closest one), even if that config doesn't match the file in its globs.

  • #1861 c45f28a - Fix running parallel tasks for a single glob, when tasks are created by a function. Nesting one level of arrays inside an array of tasks will result in the inner tasks running in parallel. This behavior should now be consistent when creating tasks using functions. In the following example eslint and prettier will run in parallel (for all files, when any JS files are staged):

    import { defineConfig } from 'lint-staged/config'

    export default defineConfig({
'*.js': () => [['eslint --max-warnings=0 .', 'prettier --list-different .']],
})

  • #1859 f0ea69d - Various performance improvements from skipping redundant internal Git calls.

  • #1856 69d7d17 - Partially staged changes are hidden in a uniquely-named patch file to avoid multiple invocations of lint-staged overwriting it. This makes it safer to run lint-staged in multiple worktrees at the same time.

title: chore(backend): cap rust files at 300 lines, tests in sibling files, split the large ones
body:
Owner rule (2026-09-24, tightened 2026-09-25): **keep files small, under 300 lines.** Split code into sub-modules and files so no file grows huge. Smaller files are easier to review, manage and keep organised.

**Scope: the Rust backend (`apps/desktop/src-tauri`).** TS/TSX (extension `bridge.ts`/`background.ts`, renderer, packages) is a follow-up once the backend is done.

## Today
- `tests/architecture.rs` rule R8 has a hard cap of 1,400 lines (600 soft) per non-test file. Several files sit at 1,399–1,401 and get trimmed just enough to pass.
- **Tests mostly live inline** (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` at the bottom of the file), so much of a file's size is tests. A few files already use a sibling instead, e.g. `commands/ai_provider/stream.rs` + `stream_tests.rs` via `#[cfg(test)] #[path = "stream_tests.rs"] mod tests;`.

## Proposal
1. **Hard cap: 300 lines per `.rs` file.** Lower `HARD_CAP_LOC` in `tests/architecture.rs` and drop the soft tier.
2. **Tests out of line, Rust's standard layout** (owner, 2026-09-25, after checking the Rust Book and rustc's own `tidy` rule): the tests of `autopilot.rs` live in `autopilot/tests.rs`, declared with a plain `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` — no inline `mod tests { … }` bodies and no `#[path]`. A big suite becomes `autopilot/tests/<topic>.rs`. Test files get the same 300-line cap. R8b enforces it; the existing `*_tests.rs` + `#[path]` files are baselined and converted as their area is split.
3. **Ratchet, not big-bang.** Put today's offenders in a baseline, each with its current line count. A baselined file may never grow; the check fails if it does, and fails if a new file crosses the cap. Remove a baseline entry when the file is split (the check also flags stale entries, like the log-leak guard does). The baseline is generated by the check, not hand-maintained here.
4. **Shrink, don't just spread** (owner, 2026-09-26): every split also deduplicates (DRY), simplifies (KISS), keeps one responsibility per module/fn (SOLID), deletes dead and speculative code (YAGNI) and trims restated-code comments, with behaviour and test assertions unchanged; each PR reports its net line delta, which must go down.
4b. **Split by responsibility, not by line count.** Pull out sub-modules and test files the way `autopilot/corrupt.rs`, `found_jobs_db.rs` and `persist.rs` came out of `autopilot/mod.rs`, rather than moving arbitrary chunks. Moving inline tests to their sibling file is the first, cheapest step for most offenders.
5. Put the rule in `AGENTS.md` so every agent follows it.

## Scale (non-test `.rs` files, 2026-09-25)
**196 files over 300 lines.** Line counts include inline test modules, so many drop a lot once their tests move out. Work largest-first, one area per PR.
